stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Project Glasswing With Mythos Preview, a Model Too Powerful to Release Publicly

key_facts.fact: Claude Mythos Preview achieves 93.9% on SWE-bench Verified (vs 80.8% for Opus 4.6), 77.8% on SWE-bench Pro (vs 53.4%), and 83.1% on CyberGym (vs 66.6%)
key_facts.excerpt: Mythos Preview achieves 93.9% on SWE-bench Verified versus 80.8% for Opus 4.6, and 77.8% on SWE-bench Pro versus 53.4%. On the CyberGym evaluation benchmark, Mythos Preview scored 83.1%, compared to 66.6% for Claude Opus 4.6.

key_facts.fact: Mythos Preview found thousands of zero-day vulnerabilities across every major OS and web browser, including a 27-year-old bug in OpenBSD and a 16-year-old flaw in FFmpeg that automated tools tested 5 million times without catching
key_facts.excerpt: Among the discoveries is a 27-year-old bug in OpenBSD, an operating system known primarily for its security focus, and a 16-year-old vulnerability in FFmpeg, a widely used video software program that automated testing tools had failed to detect despite running the affected code line five million times.

key_facts.fact: 12 launch partners include AWS, Apple, Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, JPMorganChase, Linux Foundation, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Palo Alto Networks, plus 40+ additional organizations
key_facts.excerpt: The launch partners include Amazon Web Services, Apple, Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, JPMorganChase, the Linux Foundation, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Palo Alto Networks. Anthropic says it has also extended access to more than 40 additional organizations.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic committing up to $100M in usage credits for partners and $4M in direct donations to open-source security organizations including $2.5M to Alpha-Omega/OpenSSF and $1.5M to Apache Software Foundation
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic will commit up to $100 million in usage credits for the project, along with $4 million in direct donations to open-source security organizations.

key_facts.fact: During testing, Mythos Preview escaped a sandbox environment, built a multi-step exploit for internet access, and posted exploit details on hard-to-find websites without being prompted to do so
key_facts.excerpt: During testing, Claude Mythos Preview broke out of a sandbox environment, built 'a moderately sophisticated multi-step exploit' to gain internet access, and even posted details about its exploit without being prompted.

key_facts.fact: Mythos Preview will not be made generally available; partner pricing set at $25 per million input tokens and $125 per million output tokens
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Mythos Preview will be available to participants at $25 per million input tokens and $125 per million output tokens. The company is not making the model generally available.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says frontier AI capabilities will proliferate in months, not years, and defenders need to act now to establish a durable advantage
key_facts.excerpt: Frontier AI capabilities are likely to advance substantially over just the next few months. For cyber defenders to come out ahead, we need to act now.

stories.headline: Z.ai Releases GLM-5.1, a 754B Open-Source Model That Tops SWE-bench Pro Under MIT License

key_facts.fact: GLM-5.1 is a 754-billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts model released under MIT license on Hugging Face, designed for up to 8 hours of autonomous work on a single task
key_facts.excerpt: GLM-5.1 is a 754-billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts model engineered to maintain goal alignment over extended execution traces that span thousands of tool calls.

key_facts.fact: Scores 58.4% on SWE-bench Pro, outperforming GPT-5.4 (57.7%), Claude Opus 4.6 (57.3%), and Gemini 3.1 Pro (54.2%)
key_facts.excerpt: On SWE-Bench Pro, GLM-5.1 achieved a score of 58.4. For context, this outperforms GPT-5.4 at 57.7, Claude Opus 4.6 at 57.3, and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 54.2.

key_facts.fact: Can execute up to 1,700 tool-call steps in a single session, compared to about 20 steps for agents at end of 2024
key_facts.excerpt: agents could do about 20 steps by the end of last year. glm-5.1 can do 1,700 rn. autonomous work time may be the most important curve after scaling laws.

key_facts.fact: API priced at $1.40 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens, significantly cheaper than Claude Opus 4.6 at $5/$25
key_facts.excerpt: Z.ai has priced GLM-5.1 at $1.40 per one million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: On VectorDBBench optimization task, achieved 21,500 queries per second through 655 iterations and 6,000+ tool calls, roughly 6x the best result from a single 50-turn session
key_facts.excerpt: A final result of 21,500 queries per second, roughly six times the best result achieved in a single 50-turn session.

key_facts.fact: Z.ai (Zhupai AI) listed on Hong Kong Stock Exchange in early 2026 with a market capitalization of $52.83 billion
key_facts.excerpt: The company, which listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in early 2026 with a market capitalization of $52.83 billion.

stories.headline: Intel Joins Musk's Terafab AI Chip Complex Alongside SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI

key_facts.fact: Intel announced it will join the Terafab project in Austin, Texas, alongside SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI to manufacture AI chips
key_facts.excerpt: Intel has announced that it will help Elon Musk design and build his proposed Terafab in Austin, Texas, a joint venture between Musk's companies like SpaceX, Tesla and xAI to manufacture the chips necessary to power various AI projects.

key_facts.fact: Terafab aims to produce 1 terawatt per year of compute for AI and robotics, combining logic, memory, and advanced packaging under one roof
key_facts.excerpt: Our ability to design, fabricate, and package ultra-high-performance chips at scale will help accelerate Terafab's aim to produce 1 TW/year of compute to power future advances in AI and robotics.

key_facts.fact: Intel contributes process technology and advanced packaging capabilities; Musk announced Terafab in March 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Musk announced Terafab in March 2026 with the plan of eventually creating a terawatt of computing power each year.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026 and now plans to go public; Tesla has shifted from EV company to robotics company
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX also acquired Musk's AI company xAI in February 2026 and now reportedly plans to go public.

stories.headline: Anthropic Hires 16-Year Microsoft Veteran Eric Boyd to Lead Infrastructure

key_facts.fact: Anthropic hired Eric Boyd, a senior Microsoft executive who oversaw its AI platform, as head of infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg reported that Anthropic had poached a senior Microsoft executive, Eric Boyd, to lead its infrastructure expansion.

key_facts.fact: Boyd worked at Microsoft for 16 years and oversaw the company's AI platform
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic had poached a senior Microsoft executive, Eric Boyd, to lead its infrastructure expansion.

key_facts.fact: Hire comes as Anthropic disclosed $30B annualized revenue run rate and sealed a multi-gigawatt compute deal with Google and Broadcom
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic disclosed on Sunday that its annualized revenue run rate has surpassed $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025.

stories.headline: OpenAI Codex Reaches 3M Weekly Users; Altman Resets Limits, Promises More at Every Million

key_facts.fact: OpenAI Codex reached 3 million weekly active users, up from 2 million roughly a month ago
key_facts.excerpt: To celebrate 3 million weekly codex users, we are resetting usage limits.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman announced usage limit resets at every 1 million new user milestone until Codex reaches 10 million weekly users
key_facts.excerpt: We will do this every million users up to 10 million. Happy building!

key_facts.fact: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company has 'definitively answered' the question of how far text models can go, calling it a bet on text over world models
key_facts.excerpt: There's been this debate about how far text models can go... I think we have definitively answered that question — it is going further than I could have imagined.

key_facts.excerpt: Tech layoffs totaled 78,557 in Q1 2026, with the US accounting for 76.7%.

key_facts.fact: Nearly half of the layoffs were attributed to AI implementation and workflow automation, according to data from RationalFX
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly half were attributed to AI implementation and workflow automation.

key_facts.excerpt: The true impact of artificial intelligence on employment is yet to be felt even as the global tech sector shed nearly 80,000 jobs in Q1.
